method: After freezing the exact pair, returned to the English EER Appendices 1–2, 2026 cohort student curriculum, elective rules and English thesis catalogue entry. Reconstructed the ordered study blocks and credit groups and checked the course-code distinction from Dutch History. Rechecked the prerequisites and the closest historical research alignment against the official course and workbook. Compared the result with the frozen record in a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The September 2026 full-time English BA contains a 120 EC major and 60 EC profiling space. The first listed track and package are History and Foundations of Europe. The major includes 60 EC of core study, 30 EC of specialisation, 7.5 EC Writing Skills for Historians, 7.5 EC Theory of History and a 15 EC individual thesis. The 60 EC profiling space includes a 30 EC coherent minor or approved study abroad and 30 EC free choice, with an internship up to 15 EC. At least 15 EC of profiling is at levels 2–3. The English EER and explicit 2026 cohort student schedule govern over the recruitment page’s Year 2 connecting-module description. The English course list is checked independently from the Dutch case.

The first year pairs chronological study with disciplinary or methods study, with 45 introductory EC across the first-year core. In Year 2 Power, Religion and Identity, Cities and Citizens, Seminar A and Seminar B run in order across the four periods. Writing Skills for Historians and Theory of History run in periods 1 and 2 and require 45 introductory EC, as does Seminar A. Before the two-period thesis students complete 30 EC at level 3 including Seminar A. The 30 EC package, 7.5 EC theory and 15 EC thesis satisfy the 45 EC advanced major requirement. The thesis is individual and starts with a qualifying outline.

The first listed English History package is Foundations of Europe. The three verified UCR compositions are academically distinct and share all six history courses. Behavioral Economics follows methods and intermediate economics in the corrected fall placement. UCR historical research offers a partial seminar comparison, while the separate mandatory Utrecht thesis retains its own credit and entry rules.
